relationship.statement: For small swings, a pendulum's period depends only on string length and gravity, not on bob mass or release angle. Larger release angles widen the swing and boost peak speed, while heavier bobs add weight without changing acceleration.
assumptions: Small-angle limit (10 to 25 deg), where sin(theta) is close to theta in radians.
Earth gravity is held fixed at 9.81 m/s^2 for both pendulums.
The rod is massless and rigid, and the pivot is frictionless.

quantities.label: Test rod length
quantities.meaning: Distance from pivot to center of the test bob.

quantities.label: Test bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the test pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from the vertical plumb line.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration, fixed at 9.81 m/s^2.

quantities.label: Test period
quantities.meaning: Time for one full back-and-forth swing of the test pendulum.

quantities.label: Reference period
quantities.meaning: Time for one swing of the fixed 1.0 m reference pendulum.

quantities.label: Peak swing speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the test bob as it passes bottom center.

quantities.label: Test bob weight
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational force on the test bob.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var deg0 = inputs.angle; var theta0 = deg0 * Math.PI / 180; var L_ref = 1.0; var m_ref = 1.0; var deg_ref = 15; var theta_ref0 = deg_ref * Math.PI / 180; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var omega_ref = Math.sqrt(g / L_ref); var period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var ref_period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L_ref / g); var theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var theta_ref = theta_ref0 * Math.cos(omega_ref * t); var test_angle = deg0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var ref_angle = deg_ref * Math.cos(omega_ref * t); var test_x = 1.0 + L * Math.sin(theta); var test_y = 2.2 - L * Math.cos(theta); var ref_x = -1.0 + L_ref * Math.sin(theta_ref); var ref_y = 2.2 - L_ref * Math.cos(theta_ref); var weight = m * g; var ref_weight = m_ref * g; var f_scale = 0.015; var test_fg_y = test_y - weight * f_scale; var ref_fg_y = ref_y - ref_weight * f_scale; var test_size = 0.2 + 0.7 * (m - 0.5) / 3.5; var ref_size = 0.2 + 0.7 * (m_ref - 0.5) / 3.5; var max_speed = theta0 * Math.sqrt(g * L); var is_slower = L > 1.05; var is_faster = L < 0.95; var same_len = !is_slower && !is_faster; var is_same_len_diff_mass = same_len && Math.abs(m - m_ref) > 0.05; var is_same_len_diff_angle = same_len && Math.abs(deg0 - deg_ref) > 0.5; return { period: period, ref_period: ref_period, max_speed: max_speed, weight: weight, test_angle: test_angle, ref_angle: ref_angle, test_x: test_x, test_y: test_y, ref_x: ref_x, ref_y: ref_y, test_fg_y: test_fg_y, ref_fg_y: ref_fg_y, test_size: test_size, ref_size: ref_size, is_slower: is_slower, is_faster: is_faster, is_same_len_diff_mass: is_same_len_diff_mass, is_same_len_diff_angle: is_same_len_diff_angle }; }

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum's Swing?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum against a fixed reference as you change rod length, bob mass, and release angle. Watch their motion and angle curves to discover which changes the period.
lesson.instructions: Use the sliders to adjust the test pendulum's rod length, bob mass, and release angle, then compare its swing, weight arrow, and angle curve to the fixed 1 m reference pendulum. Set rod length to 1.0 m while keeping mass or angle different to verify period alignment.
lesson.goal: Only length and gravity change a pendulum's period; bob mass and small release angles leave the swing time unchanged.
